sources.excerpt: Fuzzrocious Pedals Introduces the Dark Driving v3 Pedal – No Treble Skip to main content No Treble Gear Basses Amps Pedals & Effects Accessories & Strings Pickups Bass of the Week Gear Reviews News New Albums Sheet Music & Instruction Concerts & Tours Events Columns From the Bottom Bass Players To Know Ask Damian Erskine Recording Bass The Lightbulb Moment The Lowdown with Dr. D Health & Fitness Lessons Keep It Groovy Bass Gym Talking Technique Bass Transcriptions The Brown’stone Creative Bass Lines Bass & Creativity Bass Lick Series Advanced Bass Talking Style Bassists Interviews Wonder Women Stories Behind the Songs Reader Spotlight In Memoriam Share Your Story Videos Podcast Bass Nerds Podcast Groove Podcast Shop Subscribe Archives On This Day in Bass Contributors Contact Home Bass Gear Pedals & Effects Fuzzrocious Pedals Introduces the Dark Driving v3 Pedal by Kevin Johnson Saturday, January 7th, 2023 Share Tweet Email Comments Fuzzrocious Pedals has revived its Dark Driving overdrive and distortion pedal with a third version. What started as a one-knob stompbox has grown into a more flexible tonal device that is still able to capture the original Dark Driving pedal’s sounds. The new model has a clean boost after the traditional circuit to add volume and push your amp. The Light/Dark mod, which has been made into a toggle, has more dramatic brightness and warmth. A second switch lets you “select no diode clipping to open up your drive with less compression or add in BAT46 diodes to clip with more aggression and warmth,” Fuzzrocious explains. The Fuzzrocious Dark Driving v3 is available now for $170. An option for a Germanium diode will be available for up to 20 orders. For a limited time, direct orders ship with a raspberry-toasted marshmallow candle from Uncle Ron’s Candle Shop and blueberry habanero hot sauce from Complete Goner Sauce. Fuzzrocious Pedals Dark Driving v3 Pedal Features: Runs at 9-12V – opens up a little more at 12V BAT46 diode – warm, compressed, crunchy OR Germanium diode – gutty, warm compression (germ limited to 20 units) Light/dark mode – great for guitar/bass and sharp/warm tones Separate Gain and Drive pots – sculpt the drive/distortion Expanded Tone control – DDv1/2 tones available and way wider tone sweep Low to medium overdrive/distortion level – perfect as always on tone or pushing your amp/other pedals In his time with No Treble, Kevin has met hundreds of amazing bassists and interviewed icons like Jack Casady, Victor Wooten, Les Claypool, Marcus Miller, and more. He's a gigging bassist performing jazz in Northern Virginia and bluegrass with The Plate Scrapers up and down the East Coast. Kevin appreciates all genres of music, from R&B to metal and everything in between. Connect with Kevin on Facebook and check his performance schedule on his website .
